newsitem.title: USA: U.S. bill introduced on mastectomy treatment.
newsitem.headline: U.S. bill introduced on mastectomy treatment.

text.p: A bipartisan bill to stop women from being forced out of hospitals a few hours after having a mastectomy was introduced Wednesday by several Senate and House members.

"Women are being released from hospitals within hours of a mastectomy because their insurance companies pressured their doctors to discharge them," said Sen. Olympia Snowe, a Maine Republican. "This simply is not acceptable in a country such as ours with such vast medical resources."
Sen. Dianne Feinstein, a California Democrat, added: "No civilised country in the world has mastectomy as an outpatient procedure." She and Snowe called the practice "drive-through mastectomies."

Their bill would require insurance plans to allow doctors to determine the length of a hospital stay for a mastectomy patient based on medical need. It would also require insurance plans to cover breast reconstruction after a mastectomy and follow-up care.
The bill is similar to a law passed last year that requires at least a two-day hospital stay for women after they have given birth.
"We cannot leave the matter of one's health up to an arbitrary time frame," said Sen. Alfonse D'Amato, a New York Republican who is co-sponsoring the bill.
House sponsors include Republicans Susan Molinari, Susan Kelly, Peter King and Michael Forbes and Democrats Carolyn McCarthy and Louise Slaughter, all of New York.
